51509025.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human KEAP1 Kelch domain (residues Ala321-Thr609) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) cells assessed as dissociation constant by SPR direct binding assay

51509011.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human KEAP1 Kelch domain by SPR direct binding assay

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: The SPR assay was performed on a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare) at 25 °C. The human KEAP1 Kelch domain (residues 380–602) was immobilized on a CM5 sensor chip via amine coupling. The inhibitor was injected at a flow rate of 30 μL/min for 120 s, followed by a 300 s dissociation phase. Regeneration was achieved by injecting 10 mM HCl for 30 s. The binding affinity was determined by fitting the sensorgrams to a 1:1 Langmuir binding model using Biacore Evaluation Software 2.0. The dissociation constant (Kd) was calculated from the association rate constant (ka) and dissociation rate constant (kd) as Kd = kd/ka. The concentration range of the inhibitor was 0.1–100 μM. The pH of the running buffer was 7.4, and the buffer contained 10 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, and 0.05% P20. The data were corrected for non-specific binding by subtracting the response from a reference flow cell without immobilized protein.

51509018.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human KEAP1 by SPR direct binding assay

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: The SPR assay was performed on a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare) at 25 °C. Human KEAP1 protein (10 μg/mL) was immobilized on a CM5 sensor chip via amine coupling. The running buffer was HBS-EP+ (10 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 3 mM EDTA, 0.005% P20, pH 7.4). The inhibitors were diluted in the running buffer to concentrations ranging from 0.1 to 100 μM and injected at a flow rate of 30 μL/min for 120 s, followed by a dissociation phase of 120 s. The regeneration step was performed with 10 mM glycine-HCl (pH 2.0) for 30 s. The binding responses were analyzed using Biacore T200 evaluation software. The data were fitted to a 1:1 Langmuir binding model to determine the dissociation constant (Kd).
